issues.detail: prompt_to_repeat contains '<<제목>>', so any answer that repeats the prompt passes detectable_format:title even without an email title. Same in English ('<<title>>').

Forbidden list has only Hangul forms; prompt keeps the English title, so an answer quoting 'Getting Back Together' or writing 'Taylor Swift' passes. English forbids these. Add 'taylor','swift','together' to kwargs and prompt.
'bad' rendered as '불량' (defective/delinquent), not the natural rubric word '나쁜/나쁨'; an answer using '나쁜' passes. Prompt and kwargs agree, but the English constraint is weakened.
prompt_to_repeat contains '쉼표(,)', so the mandated verbatim repeat puts an ASCII comma in the response and punctuation:no_comma fails strict. English repeat text has no comma. Loose passes.
Forbidden '미친' is a substring of '영향을 미친다/미친', routine in an academic paper; a faithful answer fails. Verified: '영향을 미친다' fails the checker.
'슬픈', '미친' are inflected forms, not stems: '슬픔', '슬프다', '미쳤다' pass, weakening the ban.
Topic is the president's stress but '스트레스' is forbidden; answer must use 압박/중압감. English has the same tension ('stressed' vs 'stress').
'room'→'침실' (bedroom) and 'law'→'법률' are narrower than the English; '방', '법' pass. Defensible since '방'/'법' collide with 방법/방송, but the ban is weaker.
Korean adds '정확히 두 번' (exactly twice); checker is at least 2, so a 3-highlight answer violates the Korean prompt yet passes. English 'twice' does not say 'exactly'.
'좋은' is an inflected form, not a stem: '좋습니다', '좋아요', '좋다' pass though they mean 'good'. Verified with checker. Consider stem '좋' or list forms.
